package_assumption: MC9S12T64 80-pin LQFP, top view, conditional on physical chip identification. CPU/register evidence fits this family; chip marking has not been supplied.
connector_policy: All 26 manual connector positions are inventoried separately using upper/lower drawing coordinates. OEM cavity numbers and view-side convention are not printed; function links are not measured board continuity.

ecu_connector.target_scope: Manual reference for 2004 XT660R/X, correlated with the supplied 2005-labelled image; exact ECU part number is unconfirmed.
ecu_connector.orientation: As drawn in the manual, with the small tab symbol above. The inspected drawing does not state mating-face versus wire-entry view. Do not mirror or assign OEM numbers without establishing that view.
ecu_connector.coordinate_policy: U01-U13 and L01-L13 mean upper/lower row, counted left to right in the printed drawing. They are research coordinates, not Yamaha cavity numbers.
ecu_connector.link_policy: Function corroborated joins manual circuit evidence to recovered firmware behavior. Candidate association is weaker. Unresolved alternatives lists possible inputs, not an electrical join to both pins. No connector-to-MCU board continuity has been measured.

slots.path: The drawing joins ECU L/W to the starter-relay/cut-off relay network. Filtered PB1 drives the debounced 0x0880 bit 0 state at 0xCBEF; that state participates in fault-19 and headlight suppression paths. This supports a starter-request interpretation, but the L/W-to-PB1 board route is not verified.

The manual explicitly calls Y/L the immobilizer-to-ECU signal lead (PDF page 444); page 462 also joins the meter. SCI1 handles the recovered dashboard/authentication exchanges. RX/TX are logical sides of that function, not two direct connections to the harness. Transceiver wiring and line voltage remain unverified.
Manual signal Y/G; diagnostic 08 selects ATD5. Protection/conditioning lies between terminal and PAD5.

Manual ECU-side W; diagnostic 07 and timer-2 counter identify PT2. Sensor-side wire is P; external input conditioning is not mapped.
Manual ECU-side Gy; crank capture uses PT1/TC1. The sensor-side lead is L/Y and its return joins the harness return network. Comparator/protection route is not mapped.

The manual supplies TPS, MAP, lean-angle and speed sensors from L. This is a board supply rail, not an identified MCU GPIO output; no regulator or reference-pin connection is established.
Manual Br/R runs from ECU to the air-induction solenoid; R/W is its separate supply. Diagnostic 48 commands PP1/PWM1 at PTP bit 1. An unidentified power driver lies between MCU and harness.
The manual shows R entering the ECU from the vehicle power network. Internal regulation and its MCU supply destinations are not mapped; this is not a direct MCU supply-pin assignment.

Manual ECU R/B runs to the injector control terminal; R/L supplies the injector separately. Diagnostic 36 commands PT6/TC6. A power driver lies between MCU and harness. Other R/B wires elsewhere in the harness are not this ECU net.
Manual O runs to the ignition coil primary; diagnostic 30 commands PT3/TC3. A coil power driver separates the MCU command from this terminal.

B/Y joins the relay/diode network. The previous fixed PB0 association is withdrawn: fault 19 explicitly names L/B instead. PB0 and PB4 are alternative logical-input candidates, not a claim that this wire joins both MCU pins. The shared neutral/clutch/sidestand paths prevent a direct switch label without resolving the board route.

PA5/PA6/PA7 are inputs (DDRA=0x1F) read together as PORTA & 0xE0. With 0x08B1 bit 0x80 set and a repeated matching read: 0x80 invokes the full-range checksum test; 0x00 enters an interrupt-masked infinite loop; 0x40 enters a destructive RAM-pattern test (0x5555 / 0xAAAA over 0x0800–0x0FFE). Other patterns do not enter these tests. These are application service/test selections, not the MCU hardware mode pins. External straps or test-point routing are unconfirmed.
